observations: Metallic gas cylinder with integrated top handles.
Red label with 'CEPSA' and 'BUTANO' text visible in photo 1.
Blue clip-on regulator and orange hose attached in photo 0 and 2.
Stamped markings on the top collar include 'TARA 11.0kg' in photo 1.
The cylinder body appears to be brushed metal, possibly stainless steel or aluminum.

claims.evidence: Photo 1 shows the CEPSA brand, which is a Spanish energy company.
The photos show a metallic finish consistent with stainless steel, but no material stamp is visible to confirm.
The capacity stamp is not legible, although the 'TARA 11.0kg' stamp in photo 1 is consistent with a cylinder of this size.

claims.claim: Very clean and in perfect condition
claims.evidence: The exterior appears clean, but internal condition and valve functionality cannot be confirmed from photos.
Safety depends on the age of the cylinder and the integrity of the seals, which requires physical inspection.

risks.risk: The cylinder may be past its expiry or re-test date.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the date stamp on the collar or base ring.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as an expired unit (scrap value).

risks.risk: The valve may leak or be faulty.
risks.proof: A video showing the valve being opened/closed and a soap-bubble test for leaks.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as having a faulty valve requiring replacement.

risks.risk: The clip-on valve type may not be compatible with standard Nigerian screw-on regulators.
risks.proof: A photo of the valve head with the blue regulator removed.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as requiring an additional adapter or specific regulator.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the stamped expiry or manufacture date on the collar.
Photo of the valve head with the blue regulator removed to confirm the connection type.
Video of the cylinder being weighed or a clear photo of the capacity stamp.
response.reason: The item is identified as a CEPSA brand cylinder. It can be priced at its worst-case value (expired/faulty valve) until further proof is provided.
